html:
The Privilegium Minus was a charter issued by the emperor Frederick Barbarossa in 1156 that raised Austria from a march, a border county, to a duchy of the Holy Roman Empire.

Austria had been ruled since 976 by the Babenberg family as a frontier zone against the Magyars. Barbarossa took Bavaria from the Babenberg duke Henry Jasomirgott to make peace with a rival family, and gave him Austria as a duchy in return, with unusual rights, including inheritance through daughters.

Henry made Vienna his seat, and it grew into a major city. When the Babenbergs died out in 1246, the duchy was fought over until the Habsburgs won it at the Marchfeld in 1278. Austrians often count 1156 as the start of their state. See Austria.
sum: The Privilegium Minus was a charter issued by the emperor Frederick Barbarossa in 1156 that raised Austria from a march, a border county, to a duchy of the Holy Roman Empire.
